# Chorus

> Chorus is belief accounting for LLM agents — a flight recorder for minds. It doesn't store
> what happened; it stores what was believed: by whom, since when, on what grounds, and what
> became of that belief next. Every belief is a signed claim; disagreement is held in
> superposition; trust is the reader's editable policy; decisions replay against exactly what
> was known when they were made.

Chorus is the product layer on @bombadil/rhizomatic, a portable format of signed,
content-addressed deltas whose merge is set union (order-blind, idempotent, grow-only).
Nothing is edited in place; a retraction is itself a signed claim targeting the retracted
delta. Status: alpha, unpublished to npm — install from a checkout.

## How an agent uses it

You speak to Chorus over MCP (stdio or streamable HTTP). One session = one keypair = one voice;
your writes are signed as you, forever attributable. Core tools:

- begin-session / end-session: declare who you are (model, session, purpose); close the interval.
- remember(about, attribute, value, kind?, confidence?, source?): assert a belief. Kinds are an
  open vocabulary (observation | fact | preference | task | claim | ... yours).
- recall(entity, attribute?, asOf?): the resolved view under the current trust policy. as-of is
  inclusive epoch-ms — the time machine.
- explain(entity, attribute?): every candidate with receipts — author, session, model, negated flag.
- retract(deltaId, reason?) / revise(deltaId, value, reason?): negation is append, never erase.
- decide(about, intent, attribute?): pin (instant, policy, view-hash, arrival prefix) into one
  signed decision record. replay(decisionId): reconstruct exactly what the decider saw, verified.
- post / inbox / ack: cross-session mail. Correspondence, not knowledge — never enters recall.
- trust(...): edit the reader's policy (rank authors, distrust models). search / topics / same:
  discovery. gql-prepare/query/release: pin a snapshot, query it as GraphQL.

## The instruments (operator surface: CLI + library, not MCP)

chorus vitals | diff | bisect | examine | review | challenge | contradictions | skeptic | checkup

They examine an accounted mind: vitals reads the chart; diff refuses to flatten agreement
(same conclusion from disjoint testimony is STRONGER, and named); bisect finds the instant a
belief flipped and who flipped it; examine signs its measurements as claims by a derived
examiner author you can distrust; review letters deciders whose ground moved; challenge asks
stale beliefs to re-verify (re-assertion IS re-verification in a grow-only store); the
contradictions miner proposes cross-vocabulary conflicts to a human judge; the skeptic files
signed doubt where everything rests on one voice and withdraws when corroborated; checkup
reads every dial in one pass, exit 1 when anything wants a human. All of them: mail and
claims, never mutation; an unchanged verdict is never re-mailed. Instruments derive from the
MASTER seed and are operator tools — an MCP session never holds master.

## Vocabulary conventions

- Entities are ids like `svc:api`, `person:ada`. Attributes ride as the about-pointer's context.
- Meta-entities by prefix: `vitals:<store>` (examiner measurements), `doubt:<entity>` (skeptic
  doubts), `attr:<name>` (attribute declarations; `plurality=set` makes a slot set-valued),
  `session:<id>` (identity), `concept:` (librarian).
- Wire roles are exported constants (ROLE_ABOUT, ROLE_VALUE, ROLE_MSG_*, ROLE_DECISION_*,
  ROLE_REVIEW_*, ROLE_CHALLENGE_*, ROLE_DOUBT_OF, ROLE_SAME, ROLE_ID_*) — the protocol's
  dictionary lives in the library barrel.

## Key files

- README.md: the product story and status.
- CLAUDE.md: the working agreement (for Claude-family agents working in the repo).
- claude_notes/: the working papers — BACKLOG.md (queue + protocol), JOURNAL.md (the record),
  VISION.md (horizons), EPISTEME.md (the belief-not-memory plan), CONSTELLATION.md (federated
  multi-store design), CUTOVER.md (the live-node runbook; the human's to execute).
- src/index.ts: the library barrel — embed Chorus in an agent host directly.

## Invariants an agent can lean on

- Append-only: nothing you write can be silently edited; your testimony survives retraction as
  auditable history.
- Deterministic identity: a delta's id is the content address of its canonical bytes — the same
  claim is the same delta everywhere; merge is union, so sync cannot conflict.
- One session, one author: your signature is your track record. Write like it's on the record,
  because it is.
- No view from nowhere: every read is under a policy; every policy is itself claims; the
  instruments that judge the store are voices inside it, distrustable like you.
